evidence.quote: The third Napoleon had reached Lombardy, and only fifty or sixty years had passed since the first Napoleon had begun his military successes from an Italian base.
rushed into his room to consult a map in order that he might measure the distance from Milan to Dresden.

adjudications.reason: The revision keeps the clerk measuring Milan to Dresden, which the plan lists as essential. It has cut the only sentence that explains why: Napoleon III was in Lombardy, and the first Napoleon had begun his successes from an Italian base. Without it, the measurement and Dresden's dread have no stated motive. The first draft kept this sentence.

evidence.quote: unless he could satisfy himself when and why robbery and murder were a virtue and duty.

adjudications.reason: The essential moral problem survives intact. The doubtful allies (Napoleon III), the 'robberies with violence', the monkey sentence asking 'when and why robbery and murder were a virtue and duty', and V1 all remain. The cut sentence elaborates the problem but does not carry it, so its loss is a legitimate compression.

evidence.quote: Mrs. Kuhn not only adored Italy, but she cordially disliked Germany in all its varieties.
no woman had ever driven him wrong; no man had ever driven him right.

adjudications.reason: The plan requires her description, his giving the reins to a woman, and the general law. All three are present verbatim. 'Luckily for him' still leads into her taking charge, and her dislike of Germany still undoes his German illusion. The generalization about women's moral sense is a reasonable cut.

evidence.quote: She had no unity, and no reason to want it.
in any sort of organized energy. Until coal-power and railways were created

adjudications.reason: The plan's essentials specify a 'disunited, unpractical Germany'. The revision keeps the impractical side but has lost the disunity, and with it the contrast with the 'new political and social concentrations' in paragraph 8. Restoring the short sentence the first draft kept fixes this.

evidence.quote: No law of progress applied to it. Not even time-sequences--the last refuge of helpless historians--had value for it.

adjudications.reason: The plan's requirement that Rome 'resists any law of progress or sequence' is carried by paragraph 18 of the revision, which survives intact: no law of progress, time-sequences, Forum and Vatican. The cut premise sharpens that argument but is not needed to establish it, and the word budget does not allow it.

evidence.quote: He had little to say, and said it not very well; but it was still the nearest approach he had yet made to an intelligent act.
He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness.

adjudications.reason: The young man's ignorance is still distinct from the later judgment. 'He had little to say, and said it not very well; but...' still sets up the essential phrase 'nearest approach'. 'He was a tourist, even to the depths of his sub-consciousness' carries his unawareness at Ara Coeli. The lost lines are a tonal loss, not a functional one.

evidence.quote: Browning seemed rather in place. Yet Gibbon might have gone on for the whole century

adjudications.reason: The plan's Browning requirement (the guillotine shock) is met, and 'Perhaps it meant nothing.' survives. The 'Yet Gibbon...' sentence still reads coherently after 'Browning seemed rather in place': a fitting figure, yet no one could explain Rome. The plan asked for paragraph 23's last two sentences, so the partial omission is a slight shortfall. Restoring it would push the chapter well past the word target, so it is left as a minor concern.

remaining_concerns: F7: paragraph 23's 'she gave heart and unity to it all' is still absent; the plan's 'keep its last two sentences' is only partly met.
